key_audit_matters: Revenue Recognition: Revenue from sale of goods is recognised at a point in time, generally upon dispatch, shipment, delivery or when goods are made available to the customer, as per the agreed contractual terms, when the customer obtains control of the goods and the Company has no continuing effective control or material unfulfilled performance obligation in respect of such goods.

Carrying value of trade receivables and advances: The Company has material trade receivables and advances as at 31 March 2026 which requires management assessment of collectability. The determination of allowance for expected credit loss and assessment of collectability of receivables and advances involves management judgment, including consideration of ageing, historical collection pattern, subsequent receipts, customer-specific facts, correspondence, dispute status, credit risk, business relationships and other available information.

risks: The Company has in place a mechanism to identify, assess, monitor and mitigate various risks towards key business objectives. Major risks are systematically addressed through mitigating actions on a continuing basis.
Volatility in prices of key raw materials (crude-linked, natural gas, minerals)
Stringent and evolving environmental regulations increasing compliance costs
Intense competition from organised and unorganised players on pricing
Adverse macroeconomic or geopolitical developments affecting demand
Currency fluctuations and global trade uncertainties impacting exports/imports
Risk of slower-than-expected ramp-up of new capacity amid soft demand phases
Exposure to intense competition on pricing and customer retention
Dependence on the cyclical textile and dyestuff end-user industries
Working-capital intensity typical of the chemical trading-cum-manufacturing model
Operations at the newer Saykha facility still being aligned in a phased manner
The Company does not deal in commodities and was not involved in any foreign exchange / hedging activities during the year under review
Uncertainty about assumptions and estimates could result in outcomes that require a material adjustment to the carrying amount of assets or liabilities affected in next financial years
Defined benefit obligation is highly sensitive to change in assumptions (salary escalation rate, discount rates, expected rate of return on assets and mortality rates)
Judgments required in assessing recoverability of overdue trade receivables
Timing of recognition and quantification of liability (including litigations) requires application of judgment
Impairment provisions based on assumptions about risk of default and expected cash loss rates
Deferred tax assets recognition based on judgment of likely timing and level of future taxable profits
Interest rate risk from variable rate borrowings
Foreign currency risk primarily from USD exposure
Other price risk from investments in equity/equity-oriented instruments at FVTPL/FVTOCI
Credit risk from trade receivables, cash equivalents, loans and other financial assets
Liquidity risk from difficulty in raising funds to meet commitments
Concentration of credit risk with top 10 customers contributing 64.21% of gross trade receivables

outlook.statement: The Company continues to focus on optimising resource deployment across manufacturing locations and exploring opportunities to enhance operational efficiency and output in line with evolving market dynamics. Emphasis remains on capacity utilisation at existing facilities, product-mix improvement toward higher-value items, working-capital discipline and cost optimisation.

The Indian chemical industry has numerous opportunities considering the supply chain disruption in China and trade conflict among the US, Europe and China. Anti-pollution measures in China will also create opportunities for the Indian chemical industry in specific segments.
